newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly down led by palladium.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly down led by palladium.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mostly lower on Wednesday, led by a sharp fall in palladium, as the yen's firmness against the dollar dampened sentiment, traders said.
Japanese traders also said they expect to receive platinum group metal (PGM) shipments under long-term contracts from Russia on Thursday or Friday at earliest.
In PGM futures, private investors continued to sell while some traders built massive fresh long positions in distant months, they said.
"Buying of PGM distant months by some traders was probably based on a perception that Russia will again not be a stable supplier of PGMs next year," one trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from seven yen to 36 yen per gram lower. Benchmark June was off seven yen at 513 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from 16 yen to 32 yen per gram down. Benchmark June platinum was off 24 yen at 1,328 yen.
Gold futures settled slightly lower, weighed down by weaker spot gold prices. Gold prices ranged from flat to nine yen per gram lower. Benchmark June gold was off four yen at 1,141 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $315.80/316.30 per ounce at 0738 GMT, against $319.80/320.30 in New York on Tuesday.
"In the bullion market, speculative sales and producer selling dented prices during Asian trading hours," one trading house trader said.

Traders said prices of both spot gold and yen-based gold futures had more scope to fall, as the possibility of further gold sales by central banks and the strong performance of the U.S. stock market have cast a shadow on the market.
Benchmark June silver was up 0.6 yen per 10 grams at 157.8 yen.
